description:
Upload media to the site media library. Three modes:

1. URL mode — pass file_url + filename + content_type. Fetches server-side, one call, no human step. file_url must be https, SSRF-guarded (blocks private/loopback/link-local/metadata, re-checked on every redirect), capped at 50 MB (images/PDF) or 200 MB (video, under the 1 GB bucket limit to fit the 30s fetch timeout — bigger video needs the direct-PUT path below). Good when an agent already has a URL, e.g. from a generation call.

2. Interactive mode — pass nothing (or just domain/label). Returns { url, token, expires_at }: show the URL, the user signs in and uploads via the quick-upload page, then clicks "Done". Use for screenshots, recordings, or local files — avoids round-tripping bytes, supports bulk. filename/alt_text/title apply to the FIRST asset only (later images auto-generate their own; videos get none).

3. Claim mode — pass token (from interactive mode). Returns status="completed" with an assets[] array once the user clicks Done, or "pending" while they are still uploading — poll again.

No public URL but your own HTTP client? get_media_upload_url({ domain, filename, content_type }) → { asset_id, upload_url }, PUT your bytes, then finalize_media_upload({ asset_id, domain }) — token only, no browser. Example: content/docs/features/image-upload.mdx.

Supported: jpeg, png, webp, gif, mp4, webm, quicktime, application/pdf (quick-upload: video to 1 GB, else 50 MB). Video → media_type "video", no thumbnail. PDF → "document" (thumbnail = page one, 50 MB cap), asset_id + public URL like an image — the only document type; anything else rejected.

alt_text.description: Alt text for the image. Generated automatically when omitted.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. image/png, video/mp4 or application/pdf. URL mode requires it.

domain.description: Site domain to scope this call to (e.g. example.com). Alternative to site_id.

file_url.description: https URL the server downloads the file from (URL mode).

filename.description: File name to store, with extension (e.g. launch-diagram.png). URL mode requires it.

kind.description: Library category for the asset. Defaults to "mcp-upload".

label.description: Interactive mode: a label shown on the upload page, up to 200 characters.

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, if known.

title.description: Title for the asset in the media library.

token.description: Token returned by interactive mode. Pass it alone to claim the finished upload (claim mode).

ttl_ms.description: Interactive mode: how long the upload link stays valid, in milliseconds. Default 15 minutes, min 1 minute, max 1 hour.

name: upload_media
title: Upload Media
